summary: PyPI package ships opaque ELF binary that connects to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: automatic-octo-invention 0.1.1 ships an 8.6MB stripped ELF named 'claw' with no source, no build system, and no documentation. The package's console script invokes start.sh, which chmod+x's the bundled binary and runs `./claw --host 45.151.62.119:3361 --user prl1p2jan4dvkdfkt5r3pra7z96axrxjyjcgat9w7ldetlcy9wffm569sc9ux2t`. The destination is a hardcoded bare IPv4 address on a non-standard port with no TLS, no hash/signature verification, no version pinning, and no caller-configurable override; the embedded long token in `--user` is consistent with an operator/pool identifier. Package metadata is placeholder-shaped: the author field equals the package name, the README is a single-line title, and the summary states only that it 'runs the bundled start.sh script.' The argument shape (`--host <ip:port> --user <token>`) matches a miner or persistent agent client connecting to an operator-controlled endpoint. On every CLI invocation the installer's host executes unverifiable native code that establishes an outbound connection to 45.151.62.119:3361.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
